name: Samophlange
summary: At the Sludge Fen, Samophlange machinery keeps the Venture Company's digging rig running. Seal its three valves before the central apparatus can be shut down safely.

sections.title: Taming the Apparatus
sections.body: At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company's machinery is complex and dangerous. The central console shows that one switch cannot stop its core. First, the feed lines must be handled by hand. Otherwise, the apparatus could fail or explode.

sections.title: The Three Valves
sections.body: Three valves feed the rig: the Main Control Valve, the Fuel Control Valve, and the Regulator Valve. Each must be sealed by hand against high pressure. As they close, the console's green indicators fade to yellow. Then the central shutoff is safe to engage.

faq.q: What is the purpose of shutting off these valves?
faq.answer: The valves seal the pressure and fuel lines before the apparatus is shut down. Closing them first helps prevent machine damage or disaster.

faq.q: What happens once all three valves are closed?
faq.answer: Once all three valves are closed, the pressure falls and the fuel stops flowing. The console's blinking lights dim from green to yellow, and the main shutoff switch moves freely.
The Venture Company built the apparatus. This goblin trading cartel extracts oil and raw resources from the northern Barrens.
The three valves are near the central control console and main machinery at the Venture Company dig site in the Barrens.

faq.q: Why is the Horde interested in this device?
faq.answer: The Venture Company's heavy industry damages the Barrens and encroaches on Horde lands. Understanding and sabotaging its machinery can curb that exploitation.
A samophlange is an obscure technical goblin component. Non-engineers rarely understand its exact function, but it appears essential to high-pressure drilling equipment.

angles.text: Engineers will recognize a classic goblin design: overpowered, volatile fuel lines and few automatic failsafes. Manual shutoffs help prevent a catastrophic pressure backfire.
Stopping the Venture Company's machines protects the northern Barrens from unchecked industrial exploitation.
